units.title: Verify: Config loader and health endpoint unit tests

tests.name: TestLoadFS_EnvOverrides
tests.title: LoadFS applies STORYFORGE_* environment values over YAML values
tests.scenario: Given a config.yaml with auth.token_secret 'yaml-secret' and git.token 'yaml-git', when LoadFS runs with STORYFORGE_TOKEN_SECRET=env-secret, STORYFORGE_GIT_TOKEN=env-git and STORYFORGE_HOSTING_PROVIDER=cloudflare, then the config fields equal the environment values

tests.name: TestLoadFS_MissingSecretAndDefaults
tests.title: LoadFS rejects a missing token secret and fills cookie and TTL defaults
tests.scenario: Given a config with no token_secret and no environment override, when LoadFS runs, then it returns a non-nil error. Given a config with a secret but no cookie_name or token_ttl, when LoadFS runs, then CookieName is sf_session and TokenTTL is 720h

tests.name: TestHealthz
tests.title: GET /healthz returns 200 with JSON status ok
tests.scenario: Given a server built with New from a config that has a token secret and a discarded slog logger, when GET /healthz is served via httptest, then the status is 200, Content-Type is application/json and the body status is ok

units.title: Verify: Session endpoint and token unit tests

tests.name: TestSignVerifyRoundTrip
tests.title: Token signed for id 'abc' verifies one minute later within a 1h TTL and returns the same id with no error
tests.scenario: Given secret 's1' and id 'abc' signed at fixed time T; when Verify runs at T+1m with ttl 1h; then it returns id 'abc' and a nil error

tests.name: TestCreateSession_CookieAndID
tests.title: POST session responds 201 with a 32-char hex id and sets a secure session cookie whose value verifies to that id
tests.scenario: Given a Handler with secret 's1', cookie 'sf_session', TTL 1h and Secure true; when POST is sent to CreateSession via httptest; then status is 201, the id matches ^[0-9a-f]{32}$, the sf_session cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, Path '/', MaxAge 3600, SameSite Lax, and its value verifies to the body id

tests.name: TestCreateSession_UniqueIDs
tests.title: Two session creations return different player ids
tests.scenario: Given a Handler; when CreateSession is called twice; then the two returned ids differ

tests.name: TestSignVerifyRoundTrip
tests.title: Verify returns the signed player id when the token is one minute old with a one-hour ttl
tests.scenario: Given a token signed with secret 's1' for id 'abc' at time T, when Verify runs at T+1m with ttl 1h, then it returns id 'abc' and a nil error

tests.name: TestCreateSession_CookieAndID
tests.title: CreateSession responds 201 with a hex id and sets a secure session cookie that verifies to that id
tests.scenario: Given a Handler with secret 's1', cookie name 'sf_session', ttl 1h and Secure true, when POST calls CreateSession, then the status is 201, the body id matches ^[0-9a-f]{32}$, the sf_session cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, Path '/', MaxAge 3600 and SameSite Lax, and its value verifies to the body id

tests.name: TestCreateSession_UniqueIDs
tests.title: Two session creations return different player ids
tests.scenario: Given the same Handler, when CreateSession is called twice, then the two returned ids differ

units.title: Verify: Me endpoint 401 and 200 unit tests

tests.name: TestMe_ValidToken
tests.title: GET /api/v1/player/me returns 200 with the player id for a valid session cookie
tests.scenario: Given a handler with a fixed clock and a cookie signed for player p1 at that clock, when GET /api/v1/player/me is requested with that cookie, then it responds 200 with body id p1

tests.name: TestMe_Unauthorized
tests.title: GET /api/v1/player/me returns 401 for missing, tampered, wrongly signed, expired or malformed cookies
tests.scenario: Given a handler with a fixed clock and 1h TTL, when /api/v1/player/me is requested with no cookie, a last-char-flipped token, a token signed with another secret, a token issued 2h ago, or the garbage value xyz, then it responds 401 for each
tests.detail: PASS: 5/5 subtests (no_cookie, last_char_flipped, signed_with_other_secret, issued_2h_ago_with_1h_TTL, garbage_value)

tests.name: TestSessionThenMe
tests.title: Session cookie from POST /api/v1/player/session is accepted by GET /api/v1/player/me and yields the same id
tests.scenario: Given a server built from a config with a token secret, cookie name and 1h TTL, when a session is created and its Set-Cookie is sent with GET /api/v1/player/me, then the me response is 200 with the same id as the session body
